canvas.webp.title: Canvas
canvas.webp.description:
Between 2014 and 2018, I carried a few small canvases with me wherever I went. Whenever I met an artist whose work I liked, I would ask them to draw or paint something on one of them.

Over the years, this turned into a collection of small canvases by artists including [Gus Dapperton](https://open.spotify.com/artist/6sHCvZe1PHrOAuYlwTLNH4), [Tennyson](https://open.spotify.com/artist/3Nb8N20WChM0swo5qWTvm8), [Point Point](https://open.spotify.com/artist/5L67d6oZKOOmXcBcMMJdZZ), [Droeloe](https://open.spotify.com/artist/0u18Cq5stIQLUoIaULzDmA), [Metsä](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4e6vHsG1DOc9ei7zar3ds7) and [San Holo](https://open.spotify.com/artist/0jNDKefhfSbLR9sFvcPLHo), among many others.

What started as a small habit became an archive of encounters, with each canvas tied to a particular artist, place and moment.

Luisterns webp.webp.title: Luister'NS
Luisterns webp.webp.description:
I wrote and illustrated a book filled with conversations I overheard while taking the train. 

The book is in Dutch, but the title translates to 'Listen'NS', which is a play on the Dutch word for 'listen' (luister) and the name of the Dutch railway company (NS). 
I want to thank NS for the materials and their juridical insights.

There is also a somewhat cringy interview with me about the book, which you can read [here](https://www.gelderlander.nl/mijndg/tim-observeerde-uren-en-uren-gesprekken-in-de-trein-heel-oppervlakkige-praatjes~ac2406d3/?slug_rd=1).

Paper Crane 3.webp.title: Paper Crane
Paper Crane 3.webp.description:
Paper Crane is a music collective founded in 2015 by [Kyle](https://soundcloud.com/madnap) and me. We met through SoundCloud and brought together artists from across the platform, including [Omniboi](https://soundcloud.com/omniboi), [Diamond Eyes](https://soundcloud.com/Iamdiamondeyes) and [DZZ](https://soundcloud.com/diamonds4alex).

Over the following two years, we released four albums and worked on several collaborative projects, including [WWW](https://soundcloud.com/w3col). What started as a group of artists sharing music online eventually grew into a small community with its own releases, artwork and live events.

In the summer of 2017, I joined the collective for a handful of shows in New York and Los Angeles, with support from friends at [NON STOP POP](https://www.nts.live/shows/jack) and [Brownies & Lemonade](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3XgjiFz9o88).

Artwork by [Princeling](https://princeling.net/).

DEMO2.webp.title: Democrazy
DEMO2.webp.description:
I did my MA internship at [Democrazy](https://www.democrazy.be/), a concert venue and music organisation based in Ghent, Belgium. I worked on communication, social media and the weekly newsletter, while also looking at a bigger question: who actually makes up their audience?

To answer that, I combined Democrazy's ticketing data with Spotify data and built a tool that helps the team understand their audience and predict how well a new artist might fit. I also built a dashboard where the marketing and programming teams can explore the data and use the insights in their day-to-day work.

The tool uses several anonymised data points from the hundreds of ticket buyers each week to identify taste profiles and patterns within the audience. It combines this with data from Spotify's API to analyse listening trends and predict how well a particular artist might fit with Democrazy's audience. The same data is also used to automatically generate Democrazy's weekly [Spotify playlist](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/2I5aVCoFDLMBBw49gT0xhf).

Tote_Bag_Mockup_1.webp.title: Frisse Gedachtes
Tote_Bag_Mockup_1.webp.description:
For Frisse Gedachtes, a student oranization for student wellbeing, I created a lot of promotional materials for their events and campaigns. This includes posters, social media posts, flyers, etc. 

The materials are often humorous and lighthearted, but they also aim to raise awareness about important issues such as mental health and wellbeing. 

We once got invited by [Stichting MIND](https://mindus.nl/) to an event to speak with several university and college presidents and other policymakers, and even the queen of the Netherlands, about the importance of student wellbeing and mental health. I was responsible for creating a presentation for this event, which was well received and led to some fruitful discussions. [NRC](https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2022/05/20/voor-studenten-komt-de-druk-van-alle-kanten-en-drank-en-drugs-ook-a4125091) wrote a not-so well-informed article on this wich I just [had to comment on](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/timzv_voor-studenten-komt-de-druk-van-alle-kanten-activity-6933552690501197824-IRlY?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAACsrL-IBSgsaWHoqoKV6ZAL9AbWcqFuHhk0).

The color of GIF.webp.title: In The Mood for a Vibe
The color of GIF.webp.description:
My MA thesis is about the mythical term 'vibes' and how Spotify turns vague concepts like “vibes” and “mood” into something measurable and marketable. By combining cultural analysis with data from Spotify’s API, I show how mood-based playlists are constructed through both language and algorithmic patterns. 

It argues that these playlists don’t just reflect emotions, but actively shape them, turning user feelings into data that can be categorized, predicted, and monetized. In doing so, Spotify positions itself as both a tastemaker and a system that subtly structures how we experience music and mood.

Synth.webp.title: Synth
Synth.webp.description:
For my graduation project at HKU Music & Technology, I built a synthesiser and MIDI controller completely from scratch. I designed and built the body, electronics and software myself, turning a collection of knobs, faders and buttons into a working instrument.

The controller runs on a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller and communicates with a computer over MIDI. I wrote the code to handle the controls and built the electronics around the controller, including multiplexers to read the different inputs.

The design is inspired by the work of [Love Hultén](https://www.lovehulten.com/), particularly his approach to combining functional electronics with carefully made physical objects.

Makrail.gif.title: Makrail
Makrail.gif.description:
**Makrail helps you find campsites you can reach by train.** It is an interactive map for finding campsites near train stations across Europe. Alongside campsites and railway stations, it shows useful places nearby, from supermarkets and bakeries to cafés, pubs, swimming spots, viewpoints and other places worth stopping for.

I built Makrail to make spontaneous, low-car camping trips easier to plan. Instead of starting with a destination and figuring out how to get there, you can start with the railway network and see what is waiting around each station. The map lets you explore different regions, compare places and find campsites that are actually reachable by public transport.

Underneath the simple interface is a fairly large geospatial data project. Makrail collects and processes data from OpenStreetMap, combines railway infrastructure with campsites, amenities and points of interest, and uses this data to calculate what is within a useful distance of each station. I built the backend, data processing and map interface myself using Python, Flask, OpenStreetMap and Leaflet.

Feedback and suggestions on this project are always welcome, as it's still a work in progress. You can [send an email](mailto:contact@makrail.nl) or follow updates on [Instagram](https://instagram.com/makrailmap).

Luisterns gif.webp.title: Luister'ns
Luisterns gif.webp.extra: BA CMD Project in collaboration with NS
Luisterns gif.webp.description:
**How much can you learn about people by listening to conversations that aren't meant for you?**

For *Luister'ns*, I spent hours listening to conversations on trains. I wrote down the things people said around me: small talk between strangers, conversations between friends, phone calls, complaints, plans for the weekend, and all the other ordinary things people talk about when they happen to share a carriage.

The result is a collection of observations about everyday conversations and the people behind them. Most of the conversations are mundane, sometimes funny, sometimes uncomfortable and often surprisingly revealing. Taken together, they become a portrait of life in the Dutch train.


The project started as an experiment in listening and observing. Rather than looking for extraordinary stories, I was interested in the things people say without thinking much about them. *Luister'ns* turns those fleeting moments into something you can read back and look at from a distance.


The book had a small public run in collaboration with the NS while I was studying at HU and was also featured by *[De Gelderlander](https://www.gelderlander.nl/mijndg/tim-observeerde-uren-en-uren-gesprekken-in-de-trein-heel-oppervlakkige-praatjes~ac2406d3/?referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.google.com%2F&cb=badfda9d-0760-4591-b58c-77e52eccb76d&auth_rd=1)* in an article about the project.
